title: Adding 1 to 100 without adding
hook: 1 + 2 + … + 100 looks like a hundred additions. One flip makes it one multiplication.

knows: counting dots in a rectangle as rows times columns

misconception: Adding 1 to n needs n separate additions; there is no shortcut.
objective: The learner can explain that two copies of the staircase 1 + 2 + ... + n fit together into an n-by-(n+1) rectangle, so the sum is n(n+1)/2, and use it for n = 100.

claims.source: 10 x 11 / 2 = 55; direct sum recomputed with node.

claims.text: Two staircases of n steps, one turned half a turn, fill an n-by-(n+1) rectangle exactly, so 1 + 2 + ... + n = n(n+1)/2; blue is half of the rectangle.
claims.source: Column i (1..n) holds i dots of the first staircase and n + 1 - i of the turned copy: n + 1 per column, n columns. Also provable by induction. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 11): Column i has i + (n+1-i) = n+1 dots, n columns: n(n+1), so the sum is n(n+1)/2.

claims.text: 1 + 2 + ... + 100 = 100 x 101 / 2 = 5,050; two 100-step staircases fill a 100 x 101 rectangle of 10,100 dots.
claims.source: Gauss pairing / rectangle argument (c2): 100 x 101 = 10,100; half is 5,050. The prediction options are 5,000 / 5,050 / 10,100. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 11): 100 x 101 = 10,100; half 5,050.

claims.text: The reveal quotes the largest step count the learner showed with the flipped copy, m: m x (m+1), and half of it.
claims.source: Computed from c2 for the learner's own m (Demo.tsx built state); for m = 10: 10 x 11 = 110, half 55 (c1). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 11): Demo.tsx: onBuilt(n) fires when the copy is shown, built = max; reveal prints built x (built+1) and half. m = 10: 110, 55.

recall.question: Without adding them one by one, what is 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + 20?
recall.why: Two staircases of 20 steps make a 20 x 21 rectangle of 420 dots; one staircase is half: 210.
